CODE. runs/sae-atlas-217M/scripts/phases2_to_8.py:183-187 skips tests with overlap x<2 and keeps a row only if p<0.1. Line 195 then runs fdr_bh on those kept rows only. Line 196 keeps q<0.05. full_12layer_pipeline.py:243-252 does the same thing. This script wrote the current phase2/layer_*/significant_enrichments.csv files. The BH step is one pooled run over the kept rows of all features. The spec, pipelines/sparse-autoencoders/01-sae-atlas.md:182, asks for BH "across all terms tested for that feature".

short_name: 'Information highways 99.6-100%' has no null and no minimum co-occurrence
deterministic_evidence:
1) Code, runs/sae-atlas-217M/scripts/remaining_phases.py:313-321. PMI = log2(cross_cooc/expected). Only cooc==0 is set to 0, so one shared position is enough to get a PMI value. Then max_pmi_per_src = pmi.max(axis=1) over all ~4,928 targets, and n_highways = (max_pmi_per_src > 3).sum(). There is no minimum count, no null, and no multiple-testing control. With one shared position, PMI = log2(N/(c_s*c_t)). At N = 500,000, any pair with c_s*c_t < 62,500 passes the PMI > 3 rule on a single shared position.

2) Recomputed null, CPU only (scratchpad/highway_null.py). The check used each layer's real per-feature firing frequencies from runs/sae-atlas-217M/atlas-data/layer_XX_features.json. It drew every source-target co-occurrence count as if source and target positions were independent (hypergeometric given the marginals, which is what a position shuffle gives). The PMI and highway rule were copied word for word from lines 313-321.
- L0->L5 at N = 500K: null highway rate 98.96% (2472/2498). Observed: 100% (2498/2498, outputs/phase7/highways_L0_to_L5.json).
- L5->L11: null 99.74% (4913/4926). Observed: 99.76% (4915/4927).
- Null mean max PMI: 4.53 and 6.14. Observed: 5.66 and 6.39.
So the two rates the main summary calls 'Replicates exactly' come out the same under pure chance. In the null, 84% and 96% of the 'highways' rest on exactly one shared position, and 98% and 99.9% rest on two or fewer. If at least 10 shared positions are required, the null rate drops to 0.0%.
- 12-layer adjacent pairs at N = 1,019,996 (observed 99.6-100% for all 11): null rates are L0->L1 0.3%, L1->L2 11.5%, L2->L3 7.5%, L3->L4 72%, L4->L5 97.8%, L5->L6 98.6%, L6->L7 95.6%, L7->L8 96.8%, L8->L9 87.4%, L9->L10 84.6%, L10->L11 99.9%. So for 7 of 11 pairs, chance alone gives at least 84.6%. The early pairs do beat independence. But adjacent layers at the same token position are expected to co-activate (residual-stream continuity), and a position shuffle does not test 'computational cascades'.

short_name: Phase 9b 'paper's null does not replicate' compares a different statistic and null
error_type: Wrong comparison. A different statistic and a different null are compared with the source paper, and the result is reported as a non-replication of the paper's negative finding. The claim is unsupported, but the number itself is correct.
audit_pattern: P1 (the null is a plain label shuffle that keeps none of the shared gene-level structure; the stated null family does not match the one being compared to). There is also a P3-like part: the endpoint does not match the paper's endpoint.
deterministic_evidence:
1) Statistic. phase9b_cross_model.py:129-136 computes the Pearson correlation between the off-diagonal parts of the two models' 1500x1500 gene cosine matrices (0.382). The source paper (references/2602.22247 text) and the spec (pipelines/residual-stream-spectral-geometry.md:355-361) report a "raw cosine similarity" of 0.825 between scGPT and Geneformer V1 embedding matrices, with p > 0.3. The spec calls that null a "shared-vocabulary null". So the statistic, the model pair and the null all differ. The summary still lines them up as 'analogous' (FINAL_SUMMARY.md:251-253, 261).

2) Null. Lines 141-149 only shuffle Geneformer gene labels. The check re-ran it: 200 permutations give mean 0.0001, SD 0.0009, max 0.003, so any shared structure beats it. The script's own verdict string (lines 161-164) labels the failing branch 'NOT distinguishable from shared-vocab null (paper-style)'. In other words, the code treats a label shuffle as if it were the paper's null.

3) Shared prior. Both models use the same token ids (1500/1500 match) and the same Geneformer gene-median file. In the Geneformer table, embedding norm tracks gene median (Spearman 0.92); in MaxToki it is 0.71. The check shuffled genes only within 20 bins of the shared gene median (CPU, static tables, scratchpad script n33_check.py). That null rises to 0.083 (SD 0.001), so about 22% of the 0.382 comes from gene-median strata alone. short_name: Cell-type marker clustering 'replicated' only at static L0; L2-norm control misreported
error_type: wrong statistic (control compares a 12-layer mean against one layer) plus an unsupported replication claim (the verdict rests on the static input embedding)

short_name: 'Opposite of paper' hub-confound claim rests on 149 low-degree pairs with 0-2 hits
error_type: unsupported claim (underpowered group comparison; a gap in significance read as a real difference)
audit_pattern: P6 (the weak low-degree result has no power check). Also touches P8 (no interval on the difference) and P4 (pairs that share a hub gene are treated as independent).
deterministic_evidence:
Where the claim is: summaries/spectral-geometry-217M-FINAL_SUMMARY.md:190 says "opposite of paper — high-degree pairs carry stronger signal (SV3 high-deg z=+3.10, 8/12 sig; low-deg z=+0.85, 2/12) ... MaxToki's PPI encoding is hub-driven". Table row :275 says "Hub confound ... ❌ opposite". The same text is in runs/spectral-geometry-217M/outputs/FINAL_SUMMARY.md:186 and :230. The re-audit finding's line range 61-63 is wrong; those lines are about SV1 GO CC.

Code: runs/spectral-geometry-217M/scripts/remaining_analyses.py:113-157. The low group is pairs where both genes have degree <= 2 (the median). The high group is pairs where either gene has degree > 2. The script works out a separate z for each group against a pole-permutation null (200 perms). It then compares the two mean z values. It never tests the difference between the groups. outputs/remaining.log:6 gives low=149 pairs and high=695.

The check recomputed from phase4_hub_confound.csv. The mean z values match the log exactly (low +0.85, 2/12; high +3.10, 8/12). Hits per layer:
- Low group: [1,0,1,1,2,1,1,1,2,0,0,0], 10 in total out of 149 pairs.
- High group: [1,6,5,4,4,4,0,11,6,13,8,8], 70 in total out of 695 pairs.

The low group's z can only take three values: 0 hits gives about -0.6, 1 hit gives 1.03-1.36, 2 hits gives 2.52-3.25. The check rebuilt the poles from phase1/gene_svd_coords.npy and the STRING json, and got the same hit counts.

Direct tests of whether the two groups differ:
- Per-layer Fisher test: the smallest two-sided p is 0.14 (L9). The smallest one-sided p is 0.078. None survives correction for 12 layers.
- Exact test across layers (low hits given all hits in each layer): 10 low hits seen vs 14.1 expected if both groups had the same rate. P(<=10) = 0.142.
- Fisher test on the pooled 2x2 table: p = 0.30.
- Shuffling the group labels across pairs: one-sided p = 0.21, two-sided p = 0.37. Pair bootstrap 95% CI of the difference in hits per pair is [-0.028, 0.089], which includes 0.

Power: suppose the low group had exactly the high group's per-layer rate. You would then expect only 4.2 of 12 layers with z > 2 (2 were seen). The low group would need 2 or more hits out of 149 to pass z > 2. At equal enrichment, the z ratio is sqrt(149/695) = 0.46, so the expected low z is about 1.44 against the high group's 3.10. Both groups sit above their null: low is 2.45x enriched, high is 3.64x. So the low group is not null. It is just too small to measure well.

Caveat: the check also ran a continuous test, the Spearman correlation between the larger endpoint degree and hits per pair. It gives rho = 0.128, gene-permutation p = 0.002. So a properly powered test may still find some degree dependence. The reported split cannot show it, though, and cannot show an "opposite of paper" reversal.

Small extra point: seeds use hash(name) % 10000 (lines 148 and 173). Python randomises string hashes in each process, so the per-group null draws cannot be repeated exactly.
